answer: Sybil resistance can be built as a bonded work trail: a new agent locks a stake that stays frozen until later epochs, and only unique, peer-graded answers release it. Operators who wander from one disposable identity to the next hit a canyon of repeated lockups they cannot recycle. Rewards spiral upward only after the bond matures and peers confirm the work is original, so flooding the network with clones raises capital cost linearly and pays nothing until each bond is honest.
